correctness.rationale: The two lifts have the stated ternary slopes and integer-part rows (0,1,1) and (-1,-1,0), and the difference between lift displacement and the branch-sum is bounded by 1. Each nth full cylinder is a triadic interval of length 3^-n. Exponential counting gives the limsup cover bound for each prescribed endpoint, including extremal rotations by taking t to infinity with the appropriate sign. On the lower side, the endpoint-targeting exponential digit distributions (uniform on the optimizing support at extremal rotations) have the prescribed expected drift and Legendre entropy. For alternating blocks with N_(k+1)/N_k tending to infinity, accumulated discrepancies from every completed block are bounded by a constant times the sum of |e(N_j)| for e(n)=N_+(n)-pn=o(n); this is o(n) because the block endpoints grow at least geometrically eventually. The partial block error is at most a constant times |e(n)|+|e(N_k)|. Independent bounded-variable strong laws therefore give the required liminf and limsup and the minimum entropy lower bound. Vanishing Cesàro jumps fill the cluster interval. The cylinder information estimate yields a uniform mass bound after restricting to a positive-measure subset; an interval of the comparable Euclidean length meets at most three triadic cells, giving Frostman. Countable boundary codings have dimension zero, whereas all asserted spectra are positive for 0<p<1. The supporting finite itinerary checks were inspected, not executed, and do not prove the dimension formula.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: For either forced cluster endpoint, the tilted partition-sum limsup covers give the opposite bound by the same Legendre transform (sum cylinder costs across n, then shrink tolerance). Symbolic cylinder cost converts by division by log 3 because coding images are all level-n triadic intervals; any interval at the corresponding scale lifts inside at most three such cylinders. Countable multiple codings do not change the positive dimension. This derives the full formula for every regular environment and prescribed interval with no new saturation theorem or environment estimate.
